grammar.label: gradable and ungradable adjectives and their modifiers
grammar.meaning: how far an adjective can be turned up or down

explanation.en: 'Cold' is gradable, so it takes 'very cold'. 'Freezing' is already the top, so it takes 'absolutely freezing', not 'very freezing'. The same split separates 'tired/exhausted', 'good/perfect', 'big/enormous'. 'Quite' is the trap: with a gradable adjective it weakens, with an ungradable one it means 'completely'.
explanation.uz: 'cold' darajalanadi — 'very cold'. 'freezing' eng yuqori nuqta — 'absolutely freezing'. 'quite' — tuzoq: darajalanadigan sifat bilan kuchsizlantiradi, darajalanmaydigani bilan 'butunlay' degan ma'no beradi.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida 'juda' deyarli har qanday sifat bilan keladi, ingliz tilida esa bu farq qat'iy.

grammar.label: adjective order in a stacked noun phrase
grammar.form: opinion + size + age + shape + colour + origin + material + purpose + noun
grammar.meaning: the fixed order English uses when adjectives pile up

explanation.en: English fixes the order without teaching it: 'a lovely large old round brown Uzbek wooden serving dish'. Native speakers cannot state the rule but hear a break in it at once. Three adjectives is usually the practical limit before a reader stops.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida sifatlar tartibi qat'iy: fikr — o'lcham — yosh — shakl — rang — kelib chiqish — material — maqsad. Amalda uchtadan ortiq sifat qo'yilmaydi.

grammar.positive_example: She bought a beautiful old silk scarf.
grammar.negative_example: She bought a silk old beautiful scarf.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida tartib erkinroq; ingliz tilidagi ketma-ketlikni yodlab, mashq bilan avtomatlashtirish kerak.

body.text: Neither can I in one sentence. Read it aloud. Your ear knows the order.

body.text: Page six has 'a very comprehensive list'.

body.text: Comprehensive already leaves nothing out. Either the list is comprehensive or it is partial.
